identity_origin: All object identities and change numbers below are researcher-created; they are not upstream identities or releases.
ordering: Controlled evidence presentation; retrospective facts are not live event times.

facts.meaning: On 8/25 main merged #2698, whose commit body calls it a streaming-format migration pipeline
The same day main merged #3054, whose body reverts that migration pipeline; the reason is unknown
On 9/6 main merged #3585, a later streaming-migration implementation; correspondence and reuse with the earlier attempt are unknown
The design note author reports that one 116 MB session exhausted a 16 GB Node process during whole-file conversion
The recorded arrangement uses per-session stateful conversion stages, keeps committed format files and publishes only the final current generation
LogicalSession storage rebuild remains proposed: stages 1 and 2 are draft work complete, stage 3 records implementation and remote CI but is still draft, stages 4 and 5 are incomplete
The early explanation attributed the self-hosted Windows readiness failure to prompt-tail delay and cited the delivered waiting-grace fix
A later comparison reports 20.8 seconds both before and after the fix; waiting grace did not solve this failure
Direct probing found the host console rewrites the tail format after scrolling, so an already-arrived non-prefix string cannot satisfy the wait condition
Windows PTY switched to node-pty with bundled OpenConsole; seven prompts in the same sequence were normal only as an author report
Retaining the desktop package's bundled OpenConsole and conpty.dll became a terminal-allocation prerequisite; other Windows hosts and POSIX have separate scope
LibreOffice kit independently owns API, engine, tests and release; Harness owns adaptation, authorization, conversion lifecycle and UI, and locks the exact npm version
Desktop ships interpreter and libraries as a release-bound payload, records version and locked input digest, stages completion before replacing; system interpreter choice remains with the user
Conversion limits do not cover engine RSS or outputs retained by callers; desktop signature checking and final run checking are separate; run success follows the author test record
